questions.prompt: What is a branch in Git?

options.text: A full copy of your project files
A lightweight, movable pointer to a commit
A snapshot of the staging area

questions.explanation: A branch is just a small movable pointer to a commit. Creating one copies nothing, which is why branching is instant.

questions.prompt: What does HEAD normally point to?

options.text: The oldest commit in the repository
The branch you currently have checked out

questions.explanation: HEAD is the pointer to your current branch — 'you are here'. When you commit, the branch HEAD points to advances.

questions.prompt: Which statements about branches are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Creating a branch does not copy your files
git switch -c creates a branch and switches to it
Branches are cheap because they are just pointers
git branch <name> switches you onto the new branch

questions.explanation: Branches are pointers (no copying, cheap), and switch -c both creates and switches. git branch <name> only creates the branch — you still need git switch to move onto it.

questions.prompt: To create and switch to a branch named feature in one command: git switch -__ feature
questions.explanation: git switch -c feature creates the branch and switches to it. (The older equivalent is git checkout -b feature.)

questions.prompt: You checked out a specific commit hash, made commits, and Git warned about a 'detached HEAD'. What's the risk?

options.text: The commits are uploaded to GitHub automatically
The commits belong to no branch and can be lost when you switch away
Your working tree is now read-only

questions.explanation: In detached HEAD, HEAD points at a commit rather than a branch, so new commits are unreferenced. Create a branch (git switch -c) to keep them.

questions.prompt: Match each command to what it does.

pairs.right: Create a branch and switch to it

questions.explanation: git branch lists or creates; git switch moves; switch -c creates and moves in one step.
